claims.text: MOA: paromomycin: poorly absorbed aminoglycoside (acts like neomycin in the gut; almost all recovered in stool).
claims.quote: The in-vitro and in-vivo antibacterial action of paromomycin closely parallels that of neomycin. It is poorly absorbed after oral administration, with almost 100% of the drug recoverable in the stool.

claims.text: Treats: intestinal amebiasis: kill cysts in the intestine after metronidazole/tinidazole clears trophozoites.
claims.quote: Treat with metronidazole, tinidazole, secnidazole, or ornidazole to eliminate amebic trophozoites, followed by iodoquinol, paromomycin, or diloxanide furoate to kill cysts in the intestine.

claims.text: Know: asymptomatic E. histolytica cyst passers: paromomycin, iodoquinol or diloxanide furoate (prevents invasive dz and spread).
claims.quote: Asymptomatic people who pass E. histolytica cysts should be treated with paromomycin, iodoquinol, or diloxanide furoate to prevent development of invasive disease and spreading elsewhere in the body and to others (4).

claims.text: Know: paromomycin is safe in pregnancy; iodoquinol is a 20-day course, paromomycin 7 days.
claims.quote: Iodoquinol for 20 days Paromomycin for 7 days (safe for use in pregnancy)

claims.text: Know: paromomycin: not effective for extraintestinal amebiasis; also adjunct for hepatic coma.
claims.quote: Paromomycin sulfate is indicated for intestinal amebiasis–acute and chronic (NOTE-It is not effective in extraintestinal amebiasis); management of hepatic coma–as adjunctive therapy.

claims.text: CI: paromomycin: prior hypersensitivity; intestinal obstruction.
claims.quote: Paromomycin sulfate is contraindicated in individuals with a history of previous hypersensitivity reactions to it. It is also contraindicated in intestinal obstruction.

claims.text: Caution: paromomycin: use w caution w ulcerative bowel lesions (absorption → renal toxicity); overgrowth of nonsusceptible organisms.
claims.quote: The use of this antibiotic, as with other antibiotics, may result in an overgrowth of nonsusceptible organisms, including fungi. Constant observation of the patient is essential. If new infections caused by nonsusceptible organisms appear during therapy, appropriate measures should be taken. The drug should be used with caution in individuals with ulcerative lesions of the bowel to avoid renal toxicity through inadvertent absorption.
